claims.text: Surface mechanical attrition treatment can introduce a gradient nanograined microstructure.
Introducing a gradient nanograined microstructure can overcome the conventional strength–ductility trade-off.
The initial material has a relatively uniform coarse-grained microstructure.
Severe surface mechanical attrition generates a grain-size gradient from nanograined surface layers to coarse grains in the interior.
The proposed gradient consists of a nanostructured surface layer transitioning to a coarser-grained core.
The nanograined surface layer provides high strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
The coarse-grained interior supports ductility by enabling strain accommodation.
The gradient structure facilitates strain partitioning.
Strain partitioning in the gradient structure delays deformation localization.
The treated material will have higher yield strength than the homogeneous coarse-grained baseline.
The treated material will have higher ultimate strength than the homogeneous coarse-grained baseline.
The treated material will have improved ductility relative to the homogeneous coarse-grained baseline.
A conventionally processed material with a uniform coarse-grained microstructure typically exhibits a strength–ductility trade-off.
The proposed effect is limited to materials and processing conditions that permit reliable formation of a stable gradient nanograined layer.
The effect may differ under extreme loading or environmental conditions.
No eligible evidence record directly supports or refutes the efficacy of the proposed gradient nanograined approach.
